newsitem.title: UK: London gold eases closer to key support level.
newsitem.headline: London gold eases closer to key support level.

text.p: Gold was on the defensive on Monday after early selling in Europe ambushed a tentative advance that had been made elsewhere.
Prices slid further after the New York market opened, edging closer to key support levels around $377 an ounce.
"Gold looks like it's drifting back on sheer indifference this afternoon. Silver also has fallen back, but basically it's very quiet," one dealer said.
But in early trading dealers noted active selling, part of which was on behalf of gold producers.
Gold fixed at $379.10 an ounce, compared to $379.70 in the morning and $379.25 on Friday afternoon. On New York's Comex futures market, December gold was down $1.60 at $379.50.
Prices had edged up slightly late on Friday in New York and on Far East physical buying on Monday. But the small gains were shortlived.
"It wasn't able to hold $380.50 in the Far East," said one dealer, referring to the highs overnight.

Gold's trading range was expected to be tight in the near term after last week's failed rally, dealers said. Prices had tumbled sharply on Friday after selling by gold producers thwarted the rally at key resistance above $384 an ounce.
"We're in a see-saw situation, with $380 as the axis," another dealer said. "Gold is going to struggle on the upside, but support from $379 on down looks good."
Dealers and technical analysts said they expected gold to hold above recent lows around $377 an ounce.
"If it breaks down, gold is in trouble," a dealer noted.
A breach of support would target fresh 19-month lows around $375 and then $372, analysts said.
Silver also eased back to $4.89/$4.91 an ounce, up five cents from the previous London close, after rallying to a high of $4.97 in New York on Friday.
"I think some traders went short of silver on the back of gold, but there wasn't any real selling pressure there so that led to shortcovering," a dealer said of the shortlived rally.

Silver's prospects for further upside movement were limited, dealers said. It order to look constructive it needed to surmount the stiff psychological resistance level of $5.00 an ounce, which has eluded the market for four weeks.
Platinum and palladium were quiet and eyeing gold for further direction. Platinum was $0.50 firmer at $384.50/$385.50 while palladium was $0.25 firmer at $118.25/$119.25.
